findings: Actual consecutiveness is the canonical conjunction of endpoint cut membership and absence of a strictly intervening cut. If neither K.right≤s nor s≤K.left holds, the supplied actual cut s lies strictly inside K and contradicts that definition. Thus the dichotomy is derived for every actual core child, including the immediate left and right children at s.

spanningBothChild selects the old section exactly when K.right≤s and otherwise selects the tail section. On the actual right-side branch, s≤K.left implies s<K.right, so that conditional necessarily selects tail. The two section maps preserve collapsed endpoints, proving exact interval collapse for arbitrary core intervals. This establishes injection and excludes [A,B], whose endpoints collapse to the same core point.

For a left child, monotonicity puts its old right endpoint at or before A and hence strictly before B. Row0 consecutiveness survives insertion of B because that new cut cannot lie inside the child. For a right child, tail monotonicity places its left endpoint at or after B, strictly after A, so row1 consecutiveness survives insertion of A. Every actual core child therefore maps to an actual both-row child; no assumed neighbor or enumeration correspondence is used.

The singleton branch is the literal duplicateInterval with endpoints A,B. Both endpoints belong to the actual row2 cut set by the two insertion identities, and discreteness of adjacent finite indices rules out any strict interior index. This is an actual child construction, not a formal additional factor.

For every actual parent row2 child J, the proof first tests J.right≤A and B≤J.left. If both fail, adjacency of A,B forces J.left≤A. A strict inequality would put the actual cut A inside J, so J.left=A. Uniqueness of consecutive intervals sharing the left endpoint then gives J=[A,B]. This proves the complete parent-child trichotomy without omitting endpoint cases.

If J.right≤A, neither endpoint is B. Removing B from row2 therefore retains both endpoint memberships and no-interior-cut property in row0. Dually, B≤J.left permits removing A to obtain a row1 consecutive child. Exact ordered-image exhaustion recovers a genuine core child in each case; order reflection then proves the appropriate side condition, making its spanningBothChild image exactly J.

spanningChildrenBothEquiv has the full domain Unit ⊕ {K // C.Consecutive K}. Its Unit branch maps to the actual duplicate and its core branch to spanningBothChild. Injection uses exact collapse and duplicate disjointness, while surjection uses the exhaustive actual-child equivalence. The value lemmas expose precisely those maps. No core child or parent child is removed from either finite subtype.

The same derived side dichotomy puts every inherited image entirely at or before A, or at or after B. As A<B, neither image can satisfy intervalContainsBoth, whose canonical definition is closed containment of both A and B. Children ending at A or beginning at B are included. This justifies applicability of the plain ordinaryLift branch later; it does not itself claim a weighted product identity.

The statements match the source both-row case and retain the row numbering inherited from spanningRows:0 is A-only,1 is B-only,2 is both. The source table lists B-only first, which does not alter the implementation indexing. No premise is added to the source domain in order to prove the correspondence.
